current_answer: AI is linked to slower hiring at some small Danish firms, but the observational study does not show AI-caused layoffs. A separate London field experiment finds that adding a sector-specific AI-related certificate to fictitious applications raised interview invitations for underrepresented women from 11.1% to 14.2% across four pooled experiments; majority-group women without that certificate received 25.0%. That is a measured shortlisting response, not a job offer, a wage gain or proof an AI course pays off. The study cannot separate AI-specific competence from broader digital literacy. Neither finding predicts an individual worker’s prospects.

catalogue_card.question: Does an AI-skills certificate get you hired?
catalogue_card.text: In a London field test, the certificate raised interview invitations for underrepresented women, but a large gap remained. No hires or wages were measured.

summary: A London matched-application experiment found interview invitations for 14.2% of underrepresented women’s applications with an AI-related certificate versus 11.1% with a nondigital certificate, pooled across four identity-signal experiments.
Majority-group applicants without that certificate received invitations for 25.0%; the experiment cannot isolate AI-specific returns or show equal treatment.
The Danish firm-adoption hiring slowdown remains an observational warning; neither study estimates an individual worker’s job prospects.
uncertainty: The Danish firm comparison is observational and its central-bank abstract and author account report different growth-gap figures (11% versus roughly 9%).
The London experiment measures fictitious applicants’ interview invitations in selected 2025 private-sector non-degree vacancies, not actual hires or pay.
The pooled certificate result varies across identity-signal experiments; the race-specific improvement is not statistically significant.
The experiment has no general digital-skills comparison or majority-group applicant with the AI certificate, so it cannot isolate AI-specific returns or equal treatment.
